# QS-CFW-9497-56 Quality specification - flange blank CFW-9497-56 (4140)

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1  
Part(s): CFW-9497-56

Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection requirements for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (4140) produced at Plant P1. It applies to all finished forgings delivered as flange blank CFW-9497-56 to downstream machining and assembly.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material | 4140 (as specified on part drawing for CFW-9497-56) |
| Hardness | The hardness range for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 31-34 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is ±0.03 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 57.2 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of laps, cracks, and cold shuts visible at normal workshop inspection |

Inspection method
- Hardness: Verify using Rockwell method appropriate for HRC scale at locations indicated on the inspection drawing for CFW-9497-56. Record the measured values and confirm they fall within The hardness range for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 31-34 HRC. Maintain traceable calibration records for hardness tester.
- Bore diameter: Measure bore diameter with calibrated bore gauge or internal micrometer at specified inspection planes. Confirm measurement conforms to The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is ±0.03 mm. Document measurement values on the inspection report.
- Weight: Confirm forging weight on calibrated scale and ensure it does not exceed The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 57.2 kg.
- Visual: Perform visual inspection under adequate lighting for forging defects and record findings.

Nonconformance handling
Nonconforming items shall be segregated and labeled. Disposition options include rework, scrap, or engineering review. Any part failing the hardness, bore tolerance, or weight requirement shall be flagged and submitted with inspection records to Quality for disposition. Corrective actions shall address root cause; records of disposition and corrective action shall be retained in the document control system.
